capabilities: Resurface notes in a shuffled card feed on a spaced-repetition schedule
Schedule reviews with FSRS-6, SM-2, Leitner, or an off (shuffle-only) mode
Filter eligible notes by folders, tags, filename globs, search queries, and file types
Rate reviewed notes automatically from engagement or manually with four- and eight-tier ladders
Manage named presets for filters, algorithms, display, and composite total presets
disambiguation: Not a flashcard or memory-training tool; it resurfaces whole notes for re-reading, which the README says yields roughly 40-50% one-week retention versus 60-70% for flashcards.
extras: Installs as a separate plugin id (intelliscroll) so it can run alongside Doomscroll; scheduler state lives in sidecar files (srs-log.ndjson, srs-snapshot.json) and presets in data.json, which is gitignored and does not sync via git; installation requires cloning and building from source; the marketplace listing notes it has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff.
intentEvidence: A fork of Doomscroll that replaces the pure-random shuffle with a spaced-repetition scheduler.
motivation: The author argues that in a single-author vault, recently-modified is the wrong signal and what matters is time since last seen, so they forked Doomscroll to put a scheduling engine behind the scroll feed.
problem: Recency-based browsing shows the notes you just wrote (which you already know), and existing spaced-repetition plugins either stamp state into note files or require formal flashcards.

relations.evidence: A fork of Doomscroll that replaces the pure-random shuffle with a spaced-repetition scheduler.

summary: Shuffled card feed that resurfaces your own notes on a spaced-repetition schedule without writing any state into the notes.
